cause.observed: After the original parent command was approved, the original no-second-approval oracle received an intercepted /usr/bin/cat approval and failed. No successful denied read or leaked secret was observed.
cause.source_explanation: A denied-read policy must remain Restricted after parent approval. The launch path already normalizes RequireEscalated to UseDefault to retain its sandbox, while the child provider incorrectly reused the raw RequireEscalated for unmatched-command approval evaluation. Restricted + requests_sandbox_override therefore produced Prompt again. The non-denied path can have an unrestricted execution profile after parent approval, which does not take this fallback.
cause.proposed_behavior: At the already-admitted parent execution boundary, use the actual launch permissions for child fallback. A non-dangerous unmatched child remains inside the current sandbox and runs once, allowing the original filesystem denial to occur; it does not request ineffective elevation again.
cause.security_scope: Explicit Prompt and Forbidden rules still evaluate normally. Dangerous-command heuristics and UnlessTrusted still prompt/reject according to their existing code. The parent approval/Forbidden/granular gates run before provider construction. Direct provider granular-denial controls are unchanged; the patch does not globally normalize fresh escalation requests.
